note: The strict rerun rule's script, scripts/mutants-due.py. Each mutant switches off one path by which a change makes a mutant file due; the judges are the self-test and the three real runs against this tree -- a header between a mutant and its tests (core/Scalar.hpp, which must make m1-12 and m1-87 due, the second only through its headers), a shader no mutant touches (which must make m1-13 due through its application judge), and a script on a ctest command line (which must make m1-15 due). A Python mutant needs no build, but the harness always builds, so every mutant names orbsim_shaders as a no-op. Not mutated: the line that adds each mutated file to its own inputs, because every mutated file here is also reached another way -- its judges are built from it, or read it at run time, or it is in the always-due set -- so removing that line changes no verdict in this repository; and mutate.py's record_pass, which only the harness itself exercises, checked by hand instead (a pass over an uncommitted tree must say 'pass not recorded').

mutants.name: a file with no recorded pass is not due
mutants.find:
if not recorded:
        return True, ["no recorded pass"]

mutants.name: a changed input does not count
the build definition is no longer always an input
headers from Ninja's log are ignored
shaders are no longer an input of the application's judges
files on a ctest command line are ignored
an expected file that is not due is not reported
